evidenceAudit.scope: Adults listed for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallstones: confirming the indication, NICE NG45 pre-operative tests, VTE and antibiotic prophylaxis. Verified against NICE CG188 (gallstone disease), NICE NG45, NG180, NG89 and Saudi MOH Protocol-015 (surgical antibiotic prophylaxis).
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Laparoscopic procedure grade per NICE examples assumed intermediate
SFDA registration not checked per drug
Local antibiogram may add gentamicin (MOH p. 1)

pathophysiology.summary: Gallstones form when bile is supersaturated with cholesterol or bilirubin. Stones that obstruct the cystic duct cause biliary colic and cholecystitis; stones in the common bile duct cause jaundice, cholangitis or pancreatitis.
keyMechanisms: Cystic duct obstruction → gallbladder distension → colic; persistent obstruction → inflammation (acute cholecystitis).
Common bile duct stones raise bilirubin and ALP and dilate the duct — MRCP if ultrasound misses them (NICE CG188).
Asymptomatic stones in a normal gallbladder need no treatment (NICE CG188).

symptoms: Recurrent right upper quadrant or epigastric pain after meals, radiating to the back or shoulder.
physicalSigns: Right upper quadrant tenderness (Murphy's sign in cholecystitis).
redFlags: Persistent pain with fever — acute cholecystitis: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 1 week (NICE CG188)
precipitants: Female sex, obesity, rapid weight loss, pregnancy

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Epigastric pain related to food or NSAIDs; normal gallbladder.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Abnormal with normal ultrasound duct → MRCP; then EUS if needed.
ruleIn.normalValue: Bilirubin below about 21 µmol/L; ALP about 30–130 U/L

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm indication
actions: Offer laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallbladder stones; day case unless circumstances need admission (NICE CG188).
Reassure people with asymptomatic stones in a normal gallbladder and biliary tree (NICE CG188).

clinicalManagement.title: Pre-operative assessment
actions: Grade surgery (minor, intermediate, major/complex) and ASA status; order only the tests NICE NG45 lists for that combination.
Do not routinely order chest X-ray, urine dipstick, sickle tests or HbA1c in people without diabetes (NICE NG45).
Discuss stopping smoking and reducing alcohol; manage iron-deficiency anaemia (NICE NG180).
Make an individual anticoagulant plan if the person takes anticoagulants (NICE NG45).

clinicalManagement.title: VTE prophylaxis
actions: Mechanical prophylaxis from admission (stockings or intermittent pneumatic compression) until mobility returns (NICE NG89 1.14.2).
Add LMWH (or fondaparinux) for at least 7 days if VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk (NICE NG89 1.14.3) — enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily (FDA label).

clinicalManagement.title: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (MOH Protocol-015)
actions: Open biliary or high-risk elective laparoscopic procedures: cefazolin 2 g IV (3 g if 120 kg or more) within 60 min of incision (MOH p. 1).
Allergy: clindamycin 900 mg IV plus ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV (within 120 min) (MOH p. 1).
Re-dose cefazolin every 4 h (or clindamycin every 6 h) if surgery lasts more than 4 h or blood loss exceeds 1,500 mL (MOH p. 1).
Stop prophylaxis within 24 h of the end of surgery, even with drains or catheters (MOH p. 4).

learningObjectives: Confirm the indication for elective cholecystectomy and complete safe pre-operative preparation.

keyPoints: Ultrasound and LFTs confirm the indication.
Symptomatic stones → laparoscopic cholecystectomy, usually day case.
Intermediate surgery: test only per NG45 grade/ASA.
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min; stop within 24 h.
VTE: mechanical + LMWH at least 7 days if risk.
pitfalls: Operating on asymptomatic stones in a normal gallbladder.
Routine chest X-ray or urine dipstick.

patientEducation: Fasting and medicine instructions; day-case expectations.
Return for jaundice, fever or worsening pain.
lifestyleAndDiet: Stop smoking and reduce alcohol before surgery (NICE NG180).
Stay active; prehabilitation exercises where advised.
dischargeCriteria: Pain controlled with oral analgesia; eating, drinking and mobilising.
Wound satisfactory; VTE prophylaxis plan and follow-up arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Post-operative review per surgical team; return immediately with fever, wound redness, calf swelling, breathlessness or chest pain.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Acute cholecystitis: within 1 week of diagnosis (NICE CG188)
Dilated duct and/or abnormal LFTs without duct stones on ultrasound
